justification: Vote 1, read-aloud as a native. Full pass over passage, five prompts, twenty options and five rationales listening for anything a professional writer would not produce. The prose is genuinely good: absolute constructions ('with the ramp down and the engines turning'), fronted objects in speech ('The measurement I will defend'), invariant nautical 'her' for the boat, and dry closers ('By the only measure the contract knows, the crossing has never run better') that read as edited weekly-magazine reportage. One place snags the ear: 'ranked knowing when the boat would go above getting across sooner' is a garden path - the reader hits 'go above' and parses it as a phrasal verb before backtracking to the intended 'ranked X above Y'. Grammatical, but an editor strikes it, and a Swedish examinee under time pressure will lose the sentence. Considered and cleared: 'takes a manufacturer's ninety seconds' (marked but deliberate and legible); 'has earned ... and has taken it' (rule plus record, idiomatic); 'the sentence Bexwarden raised herself' (raise = bring up, acceptable with a textual object); 'the fifteen minutes' (anaphoric definite, correctly licensed by 39-to-54 upthread).

findings: The two extra mesh sizes did what he expected and let the small haddock out. -> Going up two mesh sizes did what he expected and let the small haddock out. (Q1, option A)
Towing closed the meshes, so the extra size did not give a round fish its width. -> Towing narrowed the meshes, so the extra size did not give a round fish its width. (Q1, option D - the key)
justification: Vote 1, read-aloud as a native, with the quoted voice judged separately. The passage itself is excellent and unmistakably native: 'waited for the small haddock to see themselves out' (correct invariant plural with correct reflexive, and genuine dry wit), 'A whole spring on', 'turned right round the bag', 'the meshes stood as open squares under the drag', and the absolute 'a flat fish and a stretched mesh being much the same shape'. QUOTED VOICE: it reads as a real person speaking. The four sentences are short, coordinate rather than subordinate, built on generic 'you' ('The hole you measured with your hand'), anchored to the body and the deck, and carry a working aphorism ('A net is one thing on the deck and another thing down there') of the kind trade quotes actually contain. No abstract nominalisation, no list-of-three, no explanatory throat-clearing. It passes. The one composed note is the absence of any contraction ('A net is one thing' where speech gives 'A net's one thing'), but with only one clear opening in three sentences this is within the tidying that a gear column applies, not a tell. Two ear-level findings, both in the option layer. 'The two extra mesh sizes' nominalises the increase into a count of sizes present, which is not what the passage says ('went up two mesh sizes'), and it contradicts option D's own singular 'the extra size' four lines below. 'Towing closed the meshes' overstates: the passage's mechanism is that each mesh 'pulls long and thin' into a slot - narrowed, not closed - and imprecision in the key is worse than imprecision in a distractor.

justification: Vote 2, systematic sweep of the known ELF failure classes. The passage layer is clean on every class: prepositions correctly selected ('went up two mesh sizes in his cod end', 'waited for ... to see themselves out', 'get its width through', 'The second change was to the hanging', 'had not bargained for'); no article error; the invariant plurals 'haddock' and 'plaice' are handled correctly, including concord ('The plaice were much as before') and the reflexive ('see themselves out'); 'twine' correctly mass; tense and aspect correct throughout, including the causative 'He had the same twine turned right round the bag' and the past perfect 'looked much as they had the year before'. The kill is in the rationale. 'the plaice, whom the passage explicitly leaves unchanged' uses the personal relative pronoun for fish. 'Whom' is restricted to persons; the correct form is 'which'. This is a hypercorrection error a professional editor strikes on sight, it is in English-language teaching copy shown to a student learning English, and it is precisely where an earlier gate round would not have looked. Lethal, so the vote is kill. Two further minor findings: 'more plausible than the text does' compares against a subject that cannot find anything plausible, and 'a span a careful reader can point at' takes the physical particle where textual evidence wants 'point to' - which is what this same batch writes in elf-b20-004's rationale, so the unit is inconsistent with its own siblings.

findings: and one the clerk left unplaced. He set his fee of two shillings against each enrolment -> and one the clerk left unplaced. The clerk set his fee of two shillings against each enrolment (passage, final two sentences)
The five went into their second trades at a smaller premium than the first had cost. -> The five went into their second trades for a smaller premium than they had paid the first time. (Q1, option D)
justification: Vote 1, read-aloud as a native. The passage is the most compressed in the batch and holds up under the ear: 'John Ward was bound twice' is a real opening, the semicolon ellipsis in 'in 1755 to a whitesmith, for seven years again, and fourteen pounds' is correctly licensed and elegant, and the fronted object in 'and one the clerk left unplaced' is the sort of inversion a local-history essayist actually writes. Texture is dense and unfaked - two shillings, nine miles off, combed wool, the day of sealing - with no filler sentence anywhere. Two snags. The final sentence opens 'He set his fee', but the preceding sentence is a four-item list of fathers, so 'He' has to reach past four intervening singular referents to land on 'the clerk'; the reader resolves it, but only on the second beat, and naming the clerk costs nothing. In the option layer, D compares a premium against a cost - 'at a smaller premium than the first had cost' - which mixes the sum paid with what the thing cost and leaves 'the first' to be filled in as a trade rather than a premium; the parallel comparison is cleaner and does not weaken the distractor.

findings: and one the clerk left unplaced at all -> and one the clerk left unplaced (rationale, Q1, distractor C)
one held land nine miles off -> one farmed nine miles off (rationale, Q1, distractor C)
justification: Vote 2, systematic sweep of the known ELF failure classes. The passage is clean on every class: prepositions correctly selected throughout ('bound to a saddler for seven years', 'with eleven pounds paid down', 'stood in the register', 'ran its seven years from the day of sealing', 'fell three to six years after the first', 'set his fee against each enrolment', 'combed wool in the next county'); no article error; countability correct; concord correct, including the singular 'Each of the first masters went on enrolling' and the partitive 'none for any term but seven years'; tense and aspect correct, including the counterfactual perfect 'the day their first term would have ended' and the modal 'must still be running when the first term would have expired'. The kill is in the rationale. 'and one the clerk left unplaced at all' fires a negative-polarity item with nothing to license it: 'at all' needs an overt negative, question or downward-entailing environment, and the prefixal 'un-' of 'unplaced' does not supply one. Compare the same batch's own elf-b20-001 option C, 'the evidence cannot support at all', where 'cannot' licenses it correctly - so the contrast is internal to the batch. Diagnostically this is the signature Swedish-interference shape (helt/alls appended to a positive predicate), and the passage renders the same fact correctly one layer up ('and one the clerk left unplaced'), which is exactly the rationale-only survival pattern. Lethal, so the vote is kill. Second finding: the rationale rewrites the passage's 'one farmed nine miles off' as 'one held land nine miles off', which asserts tenure the record does not - a tenant farmer holds no land - and drifts the evidence it is citing.
